# Manual Receipt Functions

Reusable compute functions for attributable reports of a transfer and its full refund. Reporting records a claim that funds were sent; acknowledgment records the recipient’s claim of receipt. Neither is bank evidence or card authorization, and these functions do not move funds. Appended changes and Payment Events take effect through successful completion of the calling execution.

## Inputs and party checks

`report`, `acknowledge`, `reportRefund`, and `acknowledgeRefund` each require an `input` containing exactly two fields:

- `requestId`: the report identifier, as nonempty text of at most 256 characters.
- `reference`: the reference identifying the reported transfer or refund, with the same text constraints.

Retries use the identical pair. A matching `requestId` alone is insufficient. Each transfer or refund report occupies a single document slot; a different pair cannot replace an existing report through these functions.

The `call/channel` binding must equal `/paymentTerms/payerChannel` for `report` and `acknowledgeRefund`, or `/paymentTerms/guarantorChannel` for `acknowledge` and `reportRefund`.

`report`, `acknowledge`, and `reportRefund` also call `sameRecipient`. It compares the parties selected by `/paymentTerms/payeeChannel` and `/paymentTerms/guarantorChannel` under `/activation/parties`. Their `lead/channel` values must have the same exact identity, and their `readerKeys` must be equal, nonempty sets of nonempty text values, with no duplicates; key order is immaterial. Missing or mismatched identities reject the call. `acknowledgeRefund` does not repeat this check.

All paths refer to the document in which these functions execute, including a nested instruction’s own document.

## Transfer and refund behavior

- **`report`** records the payer’s transfer report. After channel, identity, and input checks, an existing identical `/reportedTransfer` returns `outcome: duplicate`; a different report rejects. A new report requires `/payment/accepted` to equal `true` and rejects when `/payment/closed` equals `true`. It stores the input at `/reportedTransfer` and emits `Manual Transfer Reported`, with the input in `report`. It does not record receipt or change the completed amount.
- **`acknowledge`** records receipt by the guarantor identified with the payee. `/reportedTransfer` must exist and exactly match the input. If `/payment/completed` already equals `/paymentTerms/amountMinor`, it returns `duplicate`. Otherwise, it applies the same accepted and closed checks as a new transfer report, sets `/payment/completed` to the full `/paymentTerms/amountMinor`, sets `/payment/transactionId` to the synthetic value `manual:` followed by `requestId`, and stores the input at `/manualReceipt`. It emits `Manual Receipt Acknowledged` with `requestId`, that full `amountMinor`, and `evidence: recipientAcknowledgment`.
- **`reportRefund`** records the guarantor’s full-refund report. An existing identical `/reportedRefund` returns `duplicate`; a different report rejects. A new report requires `/payment/completed` to equal `/paymentTerms/amountMinor`. It stores the input at `/reportedRefund` and emits `Manual Refund Reported`, with the input in `report`. It does not change the reversed amount and has no accepted or closed check.
- **`acknowledgeRefund`** records the payer’s receipt of the refund. `/reportedRefund` must exist and exactly match the input. If `/payment/reversed` already equals `/payment/completed`, it returns `duplicate`. Otherwise, it sets `/payment/reversed` to the full completed amount, stores the input at `/manualRefundReceipt`, and emits `Manual Refund Acknowledged` with `requestId`, the completed amount as `amountMinor`, and `evidence: payerAcknowledgment`. It leaves `/payment/completed` unchanged and has no additional accepted, closed, or full-payment check.

Each new report or acknowledgment returns `outcome: acceptedNew`. Duplicate returns append no new changes or events. Their channel, input, report-match, and applicable identity checks still run, but duplicate detection precedes the checks specific to a new record; a matching retry can therefore return `duplicate` after closure. Missing reports and mismatched acknowledgments reject.

Amounts use the minor-unit scale of `/paymentTerms/amountMinor`; no currency binding is specified here. These functions record full completion and full reversal, not partial amounts. Completed and reversed amounts remain distinct. This definition supplies no initial payment amounts or status defaults; absent state does not establish zero, false, or completion.

## Inherited helpers

These helpers are available through inheritance; their availability does not make them additional automatic guards on the four manual functions.

- `requireSameMainParty(left, right)` performs the identity comparison described for `sameRecipient`. `mapParties(declarations, mapping, parties)` delegates to `resolvePartyMappings` with no `suppliedRoles`. Resolution requires object inputs and nonempty party and declaration rosters, rejects unknown or missing role mappings, validates explicitly selected Party values against their receiver declarations, and requires every input main identity to remain represented. Bindings may name an input party or supply a Party directly. `suppliedRoles`, defaulting to an empty list, permits declared slots to remain supplied declarations; those slots cannot also be mapped. `validPartyName` accepts nonempty text containing none of `.`, `/`, `~`, or `__`. Mapping grants neither access nor consent.
- `readerGroups(readers, roster)` combines additional reader groups with party and representative `readerKeys`; roster-derived groups replace same-named entries. `transports(roster)` collects lead and representative channels. Representative group names use `role__repId`. Missing key lists and representative maps are treated as empty by these helpers.
- `accessValid(accessPaths, readers, roster)` skips External Channel transports. Each remaining transport must be a Timeline Channel and match one Timeline Access document at an `accessPaths` location: the timeline and provider must match, and that document must allow at least one alternative key from every reader group. Separate access documents are not combined to satisfy one match. Missing matches return `false`; invalid channel or access-document types reject. `accessPaths` defaults to an empty list.
- `authority(channel, state)` tests membership among `state.parties` role names and their `role__repId` representative names. `requireActive(channel, workflow)` returns `true` when `/activation` is absent; otherwise it requires `active`, valid participant access, and, when `workflow` is true, that membership check. Missing `active` is treated as false for this guard.
- `businessReady()` returns `true` when `/activation` is absent. Otherwise it requires activation not to be closed, approval for every role in `required`, unchanged agreed terms, and valid access. Its checks default missing `closed` and approvals to false and missing `required` to an empty list. `termsCurrent()` compares every document path recorded in `/activation/terms/fields` with its agreed value; an absent fields map supplies no comparisons.
